# Q3 Roadmap: Three Builds in Six Engineer-Weeks

**Source of truth for effort:** `phase3_capacity_allocation.csv`, generated by `src/phase3_plan.py`. All effort figures are **PM planning estimates** (ASM-022, DEC-008) and must be validated by engineering before sprint 1 is committed.

**Capacity shape (ASM-026, ASM-027, DEC-037).** 2 engineers × 3 one-week sprints = 6.0 engineer-weeks. If the real shape differs (for example 1 engineer × 6 weeks), the sequence holds and calendar time doubles.

## 0. Delivery-model assumptions (all must hold, or the cut line applies)

| # | Assumption | ID | If it fails |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Two engineers, both dedicated to this work for 3 weeks (no support rotation or parallel project) | ASM-027 | Capacity < 6.0: apply the cut line |
| 2 | Both can work backend and frontend; QA is done by the same engineers | ASM-026 | Sequencing changes; FE-heavy sprint 2 may slip |
| 3 | An engineer-week is a full productive week: code review, ceremonies, deployment and test-data setup fit inside the estimates | ASM-027 | Effectively less than 6.0: apply the cut line |
| 4 | CI/CD, staging and a copy of Acme data for testing already exist | ASM-027 | Environment work is not in the plan: cut or extend |
| 5 | Schema migrations (offer statuses, event log, application source) need no separate platform-team work | ASM-027 | Dependency on another team: re-plan sprint 1 |
| 6 | Design sketches are ready before sprint 2 (PM/design time, not engineering capacity) | ASM-027 | FE uses existing patterns |
| 7 | TalentFlow knows each record's creation path, so intake method is system-derived | ASM-029 | B3.1 grows: cut the duplicate warning first |
| 8 | **Every figure here is a PM planning estimate** until engineering validates it in week 0 | ASM-022 | Re-plan; scope is cut, capacity is never stretched |

## 3. Sprints

### Sprint 1: Foundations (2.0 engineer-weeks)
**Objective:** make bad states impossible going forward, and detectable for the past.

**Deliverables:**

| Component | Effort | What |
|---|---:|---|
| B1.1 | 1.00 | Offer status model and constraints |
| B2.1 | 0.75 | Stall detector and requisition-consistency rules |
| B3.1 | 0.25 | Application-level Source and Intake Method; referral validation |

- **B1.1:** adds Expired, Withdrawn, Rescinded and Superseded; enforces allowed transitions; requires Decision On if and only if the status is terminal; adds an optional Expires On. Existing contradictions are marked `status_date_conflict`, not rewritten.
- **B2.1:** the inactivity threshold is configurable per application stage at org level (provisional default 90 days for every stage, range 14–365, changes audited). Opening-status contradictions create **review flags only**; the system never writes an application or opening status.
- **B3.1:** Source = Referral requires a referrer, and a referrer requires Referral or the explicit "referred via other channel" option.

**Dependencies:**
- Schema-change review: engineering.
- No customer answer is required.

**Acceptance criteria:**
1. An attempt to save Pending with a Decision On, or Accepted without one, is rejected by the API.
2. On a copy of Acme data, the migration flags exactly the records that the reference implementation flags (4 conflicts, OAM-03c), and no record is modified.
3. The inactivity detector reproduces DQ-28 on the snapshot at the default threshold: 50/105 at the 2026-08-27 cutoff. Changing the threshold changes the count as in `phase3_1_evidence.csv`: 71/105 at 60 days, 43/105 at 120.
6. Every transition in the lifecycle table (spec §8) is accepted for the permitted *proposed* roles and rejected for others. Roles are configuration; Acme's mapping (C-17) must be set before the pilot; every status change writes an audit event; the invariants flag exactly the 4 legacy conflicts (E-B1-1).
7. No code path changes an opening's status or an application's status automatically.
4. Requisition rules reproduce the DQ-11 openings (15/24).
5. A new application with Source = Referral and no referrer cannot be saved.

**Risks:**
- A schema change touches the existing offer flows.
- Mitigation: transitions are additive, and old statuses stay valid.

**Milestone:** engineering demo of the rules against a copy of the Acme snapshot.

### Sprint 2: Core workflows (2.0 engineer-weeks)
**Objective:** give recruiters one place to resolve each kind of debris.

**Deliverables:**

| Component | Effort | What |
|---|---:|---|
| B1.2 | 0.50 | Pending-offer queue |
| B2.2 | 0.75 | Inactivity review queue and opening review banner |
| B3.2 | 0.25 | Duplicate-warning service (**first cut**) |
| B3.3a | 0.25 | Intake form: source taxonomy, referrer, endorsement confirmation |
| B3.3b | 0.25 | Duplicate-warning dialog (**first cut**) |

- **B1.2:** age buckets 0–14, 15–30, 31–60 and over 60 days; a conflict badge; one-step resolve.
- **B2.2:** the flag reads "Inactive > N days". Dispositions: still active (snooze with reason), close as recruiter-confirmed abandoned, close for another reason, or advance. Bulk actions need a reason; closes are reversible for 30 days.
- **B3.2 and B3.3b:** match on name AND phone. **Warning-only.** The options are "same person" (attach the application to the existing record; nothing merged), "different person" (with a reason; the pair is remembered), or "unsure" (recruiting-ops review queue).
- **B3.3a:** acquisition source comes from the controlled taxonomy. Intake method is system-derived and not on the form.

**Dependencies:**
- UX sketches.
- C-06 (meaning of Closed On), so that the close disposition writes the right fields. *If unanswered:* the disposition writes Status = Closed and a disposition reason, and Closed On semantics stay as they are.

**Acceptance criteria:**
1. A recruiter can resolve a pending offer in at most 2 actions.
2. Bulk-closing 10 inactivity-flagged applications records a reason on each, and all are reversible. "Abandoned" appears only when a recruiter chose that disposition.
3. A duplicate-warning test set built from the 6 DQ-02 pairs raises a warning for all 6, and for 0 name-only or phone-only collisions (E-B3-dup-*). No action merges or deletes a record. A pair marked "different person" is not warned again.
4. The intake form cannot submit a contradictory Source and referrer.

**Risks:**
- Alert fatigue.
- False duplicate warnings on common names. Mitigation: matching requires both name and phone.

**Milestone:** internal usability review with 1–2 Acme recruiters on staging. This is the first customer validation of whether the queues match how they work (C-11).

### Sprint 3: Metrics, QA and pilot release (2.0 engineer-weeks)
**Objective:** ship to an Acme pilot with trustworthy metrics and a measured baseline.

**Deliverables:**

| Component | Effort | What |
|---|---:|---|
| B1.3 | 0.50 | D3 metrics and dashboard tiles |
| B1.4 | 0.50 | B1 QA |
| B2.3 | 0.25 | Live baseline and hygiene scorecard |
| B2.4 | 0.25 | B2 QA |
| B3.4 | 0.25 | Attribution report |
| B3.5 | 0.25 | B3 QA |

- **B1.3:** OAM-01 to OAM-10, following `offer_acceptance_metric_spec.md`, with the n ≥ 10 suppression rule.

**Dependencies:**
- Pilot agreement with Acme.
- C-03 (expiry policy), used only to pre-fill a default Expires On. *If unanswered:* left blank.

**Acceptance criteria:**
1. The dashboard values for OAM-01, OAM-02, OAM-03 and OAM-09 equal `src/offer_metrics.py` on the same data, computed at event time (an accept-then-renege offer stays in the OAM-01 numerator and appears in OAM-13a). On the snapshot: 26/31, 26/36, 5 and 24/28.
2. Rates with a denominator below 10 display counts only.
3. Offer-level and candidate-level tiles are labelled and never combined.
4. Every success metric in `product_success_metrics.csv` has a working data source and a recorded live baseline.

**Risks:**
- The live baseline differs sharply from the snapshot. That is expected, so targets are re-confirmed after measurement.

**Milestone:** pilot release to Acme recruiters, and a stakeholder review with the VP of People covering the D3 metric, the pending backlog and the plan for the N1 decision.

## 4. Committed, conditional and backlog scope

| Scope | Items | Rule |
|---|---|---|
| **Committed (6.0)** | B1.1–B1.4, B2.1–B2.4, B3.1, B3.2, B3.3a, B3.3b, B3.4, B3.5, as above | Depends on no unanswered customer question |
| **Conditional** | Auto-expire offers past Expires On (needs C-03). Auto-close of inactivity-flagged applications (needs C-11, C-06). Back-fill of historical application source (needs C-04). A recruiter-initiated merge tool (needs C-07); **automatic merging is never in scope**. Privacy threshold confirmation (ASM-028). OAM-01b as a default exclusion (needs C-08) | **Not in the 6.0.** Swapped in only by de-scoping an equal amount of committed effort, with PM approval |
| **Future backlog** | N1 job-board integration (decision at Q4 planning). X1 interview scheduling and feedback-latency tooling (after C-05). X2 department analytics (when n allows). N2 and N3 only under their reconsideration criteria | Re-scored at Q4 planning with live data |

**Cut line.** If engineering validation finds the committed scope exceeds 6.0, cut in this order and re-validate after each step:

| Order | Cut | Saves |
|---|---|---:|
| 1 | Duplicate warning: B3.2 + B3.3b. **This is also the first cut if B3 alone is estimated above 1.5** | 0.5 (the intake form B3.3a and validation B3.1 are kept) |
| 2 | B2.2 bulk actions; keep single-item disposition | ≈0.25 |
| 3 | B1.3 dashboard tiles; table export only, metric logic kept | ≈0.25 |

B1.1, B2.1 and B3.1, the rules that stop new bad data, are never cut.

## 5. Milestones

| When | Milestone | Audience | Decision taken |
|---|---|---|---|
| Week 0 | Estimates validated; customer questions sent | Eng lead, PM | Commit or cut |
| End of sprint 1 | Rules demo on a copy of the snapshot | Eng, PM | Proceed to UI |
| End of sprint 2 | Recruiter usability review | Acme recruiters | Adjust queue UX |
| End of sprint 3 | Pilot release + VP review | VP of People, Acme recruiting ops | Adopt the D3 metric as the reported acceptance figure |
| Pilot + 6 weeks | First scorecard read | PM, VP | Continue or iterate |
| Q4 planning | N1 job-board decision, using B3 intake data and C-12 | PM, VP, eng | Build, defer or drop |
